checks.description: The anti-air ceiling on bounded rocket rungs changed at least one barracks decision from e3 to another body. Last fight the side saw about 7% armour (283 infantry sightings, 3 aircraft, 1 vehicle, 16 economy) and the rungs still bought 37 e3. If absent against an infantry-heavy opponent: EnemySightings never reached 6, the ceiling never fell below a rung, or the claim's baseline disagrees with the plan. Absent against an armour-heavy opponent (>= 60% armour seen) is correct, because the rule does not apply.

The ceiling keeps the DefenceAntiAirCore pair plus one per aircraft seen, and the pre-contact Opening rung (e3 x4) is untouched, so some rockets are always bought. Zero means the cap deleted the only unit that shoots upwards.

37 e3 were built last fight (11,100 credits, 8 kills, 1,387.5 credits a kill) against an opponent with no combat vehicles. Capped at 2 + aircraft seen, an infantry-heavy opponent should see at most about 20. Expect this to fail, legitimately, against an armour-heavy opponent where the cap does not apply.
e1 killed at 88.1 credits a kill last fight. Spend moved off rockets lands mostly on the rifle rungs, and more rifles must not mean worse rifles.

armyValueIntegral was the one fitness component with room, apart from survival: mean army 3,705.7 against a reference of 6,000 (4,831 the round before). e3 lost 78% of what was spent on them and e1 64%, so the same spend on rifles should hold more army.
valueExchangeRatio was 2.382 (the component saturates at 2). Replacing a unit that is swept by infantry at -0.9 should not lower it.
The change touches only infantry rung sizes. Income was 58.3 c/s (prior median 42.2), and the engine-first opening that produced it is unchanged.
